Issue Description: Notifications router endpoints lack `Depends(get_current_user)` authentication dependency.
Impact: Unauthenticated attackers can retrieve sensitive student notifications and unread health alerts by probing emails.
Defensive Recommendation: Add `get_current_user` auth dependency to all notification endpoints and verify `current_user['email'] == student_email`.

Issue Description: Schedule update endpoint `PUT /{doctor_id}/schedule` lacks authentication and doctor role verification.
Impact: Any unauthenticated user can overwrite doctor schedules and availability slots.
Defensive Recommendation: Require `get_current_user` and enforce that `current_user['role'] == 'doctor'` and `current_user['_id'] == doctor_id`.

Issue Description: Patient list endpoint `GET /{doctor_id}/patients` lacks authentication checks.
Impact: Unauthenticated users can list full profile details of all students who booked appointments with a doctor.
Defensive Recommendation: Add `get_current_user` dependency and ensure requester is either the specific doctor or an admin.

Issue Description: `SECRET_KEY` lacks default strength enforcement and allows starting with empty/weak configuration.
Impact: Allows potential session token forgery if default secret is deployed.
Defensive Recommendation: Require mandatory strong `SECRET_KEY` validation in Pydantic settings schema on startup.

Issue Description: CORS middleware defaults to `allow_origins=['*']` with `allow_credentials=True` when `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` environment variable is not explicitly set.
Impact: Cross-origin scripts can read responses on authenticated endpoints if wildcards combined with credentials are abused by browsers.
Defensive Recommendation: Set explicit list of domain origins for CORS and disable wildcard when credentials are enabled.

Issue Description: Authentication routes (login, OTP generation, password reset) have no rate-limiting middleware.
column9: Integrate `slowapi` rate-limiter middleware (e.g. 5 requests/minute per IP).

Issue Description: Profile image upload lacks magic byte/header verification and file size limits.
Impact: Users could upload arbitrarily large files causing denial of service or storage exhaustion.
Defensive Recommendation: Validate image magic numbers (PIL/imghdr) and cap uploads at 5MB.

Issue Description: MongoDB `$regex` queries with raw strings are used for email lookups instead of lowercased indexed strings.
Impact: Potential ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service) or unintended regex pattern matching.
Defensive Recommendation: Store normalized lowercased emails and query using standard exact match `{"email": clean_email}` with DB index.

Issue Description: On startup, default admin account `admin@unihealth.ai` is created with weak default password `admin123` if absent.
Impact: Predictable admin credentials if environment isn't customized.
Defensive Recommendation: Load initial admin setup password from `INITIAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` env variable and force mandatory reset on first login.
